clue.text: Channels in motorway area provide equine with water, not fresh

indicators.note: the following pieces sit in the middle of the motorway's name, so the road wraps around them

parts.note: the M1, Britain's first motorway, read as letters
an ass is a member of the horse family
the Med, a salt sea rather than fresh water

explanation.surface: A traveller at a motorway service area gives a horse a drink of stale water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Provide equine with water' puts the Mediterranean after the animal; that pair goes inside the M1, and the area's A finishes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Television, radio and newspapers are communication channels reaching huge audiences, which is what the phrase names.

clue.text: Making a pair: marrying must involve church

indicators.note: to involve something is to take it inside, so the church abbreviation goes within the other word

explanation.surface: A wedding has to take place in church to count.
explanation.definitionFit: Matching socks or colours means putting together things that form a pair, so the participle fits exactly.

clue.text: Something afoot: no time for throwing a spanner in the works?

indicators.note: 'no time' tells us a word for time is taken out of the longer word

parts.words: throwing a spanner in the works

parts.note: an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: No time is left for wrecking the works, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something afoot' sounds like a plot brewing, but it is literal: a sabot is a wooden clog worn on the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A sabot is a carved wooden shoe, literally worn on a person's foot, hence the punning phrase.

clue.text: Noble big beast heading off to follow procession

indicators.note: the head, or first letter, of the beast's name is removed

parts.note: a march is an organised procession

explanation.surface: An aristocrat watches a huge animal leave to trail a parade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To follow procession' puts the shortened animal after the march.
explanation.definitionFit: A marchioness is a woman of rank, wife of a marquess, so she is a member of the nobility.

clue.text: Timid creature concealing mark that identifies when death is near

indicators.note: to conceal something is to hide it inside, so the mark goes within the creature

parts.note: a label or tag identifies its owner

explanation.surface: A shy deer hides a tag that tells you when it is dying.
explanation.definitionFit: Dotage is extreme old age with failing faculties, the final stage of life before someone dies.

clue.text: The equivalent of first prize for behaving well

definitions.meaning: first meaning: worth as much as a winner's gold medal
second meaning: the idiom for a well-behaved child

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase is read literally first, then as the everyday idiom praising good conduct.
explanation.definitionFit: Winners take gold medals; and a child who causes no trouble is said, idiomatically, to be equally precious.

clue.text: What may be read in a church in the country?

indicators.note: the article and church abbreviation are placed inside the country's name

explanation.surface: A question about what is read aloud in a country church.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: Malachi is the last book of the Old Testament, read during services.
explanation.definitionFit: Malachi is a prophetic book of the Bible, so passages from it are read as lessons in church services.

clue.text: One soldier embraces another, before returning to old war minister

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold inside your arms, so one soldier goes within the other

parts.note: a man is a private soldier
a GI is an American soldier

indicators.note: coming back means the short word is read backwards in a down light

explanation.surface: One soldier hugs a comrade before going back home.
explanation.walkthrough: The American soldier sits inside the British one, and the little word that ends the clue is turned around.
explanation.definitionFit: André Maginot was the French minister of war who gave his name to the defensive line built in the 1930s.

clue.text: Unconventional ideas after family visits foreign parliament

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside a place, so the relatives go within the parliament

explanation.surface: Fresh ideas arrive after relatives tour an overseas legislature.
explanation.walkthrough: The Althing, Iceland's parliament, is one of the oldest in the world; the family goes in just before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Lateral thinking means solving problems by indirect, creative approaches rather than following conventional logic step by step.

clue.text: My old folk in exalted ceremony

parts.note: cor! is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'

explanation.surface: My elderly relatives attend a grand ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' looks possessive but is an exclamation, the same as the British 'cor'.
explanation.definitionFit: Crowning a monarch is a solemn ceremony that literally raises the ruler to the highest station.

clue.text: Without James I at the front, a fierce battle

indicators.note: being placed at the front means this letter is written before everything else

parts.note: w/o is the abbreviation for without

explanation.surface: Without King James I leading, a fierce battle follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'James I' looks like the king, but the I is a separate letter sent to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Iwo Jima was the site of a bloody 1945 Pacific engagement between American and Japanese forces.

clue.text: Shut up, being a century old

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for century (and Roman 100)

explanation.surface: An order to be quiet aimed at someone a hundred years old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shut up' reads as an order to be quiet, but it means confined.
explanation.definitionFit: Something shut up in a cage is imprisoned, enclosed behind bars like a zoo animal.

clue.text: Be sold as a little money passes

definitions.meaning: first meaning: pass to a new owner
second meaning: coins handed over from one palm to another

explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads the phrase literally: small coins are 'change', and they pass between people's hands.
explanation.definitionFit: When property is sold, ownership transfers from one person to another, the idiomatic sense of the phrase.

clue.text: What involve sliding, as you will hear

definitions.text: What involve sliding, as you will hear

parts.note: surface reading: something like skating or a playground slide
setter's reading: these slides are heard, being musical sweeps from note to note

explanation.surface: Things that involve slipping about, so you'll be told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As you will hear' sounds like hearsay, but it means the slides are audible, which points to music.
explanation.definitionFit: In music these are rapid glides across a run of pitches, played on harp, piano or trombone.

clue.text: Creatures put on islands

parts.note: to don clothes is to put them on
keys are low islands, as in the Florida Keys

explanation.surface: Animals are placed on islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Donkeys are domestic animals of the horse family, so the general word for animals covers them.

clue.text: Make lace to cover plain silk fabric

indicators.note: covering something wraps it, so the lacemaking word goes around the other

parts.note: tatting is a way of making lace by hand

explanation.surface: Someone makes lace to trim a plain silk cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain silk' looks like a phrase describing the cloth, but plain belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabaret is a striped upholstery material alternating watered and satin bands of silk.

clue.text: Comic's funny stagger

indicators.note: funny here means odd or peculiar, so the letters come out strangely ordered

explanation.surface: A comedian's amusing drunken walk.
explanation.definitionFit: A gagster is a joke-teller, a comedian whose stock in trade is one-liners and quips.

clue.text: One may stand for this new idea, not local

indicators.note: 'not local' says a word for local is removed from the longer word

parts.note: an innovation is something newly devised
in Britain your local is your neighbourhood pub

explanation.surface: A fresh idea that isn't from around here might win support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' is British slang for the nearby pub, so a word for pub comes out.
explanation.definitionFit: An audience rises to its feet to applaud a great performance, giving a standing tribute.

clue.text: Suggesting diner thought to start well-prepared

parts.note: these twelve letters can be rearranged into the first three words of the answer
a reverse clue: the answer's last word, read as an anagram signal, is what would turn its first three words into the quoted phrase

explanation.surface: A café customer's idea is a way to begin with everything ready.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as wordplay, 'hit the ground' with 'running' as an anagram signal, and it yields 'diner thought'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes starting a new job or project at full speed, already prepared and effective from day one.

clue.text: Drop daughter off: how I refer to her?

indicators.note: the daughter's abbreviation is taken off the word for drop

parts.note: to shed is to let fall

explanation.surface: A parent dropping a girl off at school wonders how to describe her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop daughter off' sounds like the school run; it means removing one letter from a word for drop.
explanation.definitionFit: The third-person feminine pronoun is what a speaker uses when referring to a woman or girl.

clue.text: I felt that food comes first for absentee

indicators.note: coming first means this piece is written ahead of the other

parts.note: nosh is British slang for food
ow! is what you say when you feel pain

explanation.surface: Someone who got hurt explains that eating comes before the person who didn't turn up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comes first' puts the food word ahead of the cry of pain.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-show is a person who books or promises to attend and then never turns up.

clue.text: Attempt place in event

parts.note: to have a shot is to make an attempt

explanation.surface: Try to finish in a placing at a competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Place in event' sounds like finishing in the medals, but place is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting the shot is an athletics field discipline in which a heavy metal ball is thrown.

clue.text: Colour left on stick

indicators.note: in an across light one piece placed on another is simply written after it

parts.note: to paste is to stick with glue

explanation.surface: Some paint was left on a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastel is a soft, pale shade, the kind of gentle tint used in pastel crayons.

clue.text: Various items on table in afternoon for mother-to-be?

definitions.text: Various items on table in afternoon
definitions.meaning: first meaning: the cups, pot and saucers laid out at teatime

definitions.note: describes what the items are for rather than naming them
definitions.meaning: second meaning: in British homes the person who pours is said to 'be mother', and these are what they need

explanation.walkthrough: 'Mother-to-be' looks like a pregnant woman, but 'shall I be mother?' is a British way of offering to pour.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase covers cups, saucers, teapot and milk jug set out when people gather for an afternoon cuppa.

clue.text: Fighter perhaps shows such exceptional speed over track

indicators.note: in a down light one piece over another is written above it, so it comes first

parts.note: warp speed is the impossibly fast speed of science fiction starships
a lane is a track, as on a running track

explanation.surface: A boxer demonstrates amazing pace around the running track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fighter' suggests a boxer; the 'perhaps' warns it is one example, an aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A fighter jet is one kind of military aircraft built for combat, so it exemplifies the answer.

clue.text: Western hero's individualist rage

explanation.surface: A cowboy hero's solitary fury.
explanation.definitionFit: The masked cowboy of American radio, film and television is a famous hero of cowboy stories.

clue.text: Numerous murals at last honoured unusual city fathers

indicators.note: unusual means out of the normal order, so the letters are rearranged
only the final letter of the following word is wanted

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Many wall paintings finally celebrated the strange founders of a city.
explanation.definitionFit: The twin brothers of legend founded Rome, so they are that city's mythical founding fathers.

clue.text: Cheating gangster to achieve checkmate?

parts.note: a hood is a hoodlum, a gangster
checkmate wins the game by trapping the king, so 'win king'

explanation.surface: A mobster cheats to win a game of chess.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful reading: checkmate means you win against the opposing king.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoodwinking is deceiving or tricking someone, the same as conning or swindling them.

clue.text: Flier needs a little speed to get up

parts.note: a whit is a tiny amount

indicators.note: rising up a down light means the word is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A pilot needs a bit of speed to take off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flier' suggests a pilot but means a bird; 'a little' is one word, not part of 'a little speed'.
explanation.definitionFit: A whitecap is a bird name, used for birds with a white crown such as the male redstart.

clue.text: One filleting fish maybe, good and thorough

explanation.surface: A fishmonger who is skilled and does a complete job.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who cleans fish removes the innards, which is gutting, so the worker doing it is named this way.

clue.text: Secures small pieces that have sprung up

indicators.note: springing up a down light means reading the letters from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Someone fastens down little bits that have popped up.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means fastens with a band or belt, so it matches binding or fixing something in place.

clue.text: Piece attached to heel is hanging

parts.note: a tap is a metal plate fixed to a shoe's heel

explanation.surface: A segment fixed to the heel is dangling loose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hanging' looks like a verb, but it is a noun for a wall drapery.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapis is a tapestry or carpet used as a wall covering or table cloth, a decorative textile.

clue.text: Income, including nice car, new demand from old lover?

indicators.note: including something means taking it inside, so the car and new go within the income word

explanation.surface: An ex-partner wants money, a smart car and more besides.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is loose: this is a claim made by a former partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Palimony is support payment claimed by a former unmarried partner after a relationship breaks up.

clue.text: Petulant display at sea is shifty

indicators.note: being at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A sulky outburst on board ship looks suspicious.
explanation.definitionFit: A tantrum thrown in a fit of pique is a childish show of bad temper.

clue.text: Regularly fear I invite disaster

indicators.note: every other letter of the next word is kept

parts.note: to lure is to entice or invite

explanation.surface: A worrier constantly frets about courting catastrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete flop or fiasco is a catastrophe, so the noun for lack of success fits.

clue.text: People in a heap in the garden: one's sane

indicators.note: the people are placed inside the garden heap

parts.note: a compost heap of rotting garden waste
one is I, and the apostrophe s is 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone sits in a garden heap yet insists they are perfectly sane.
explanation.walkthrough: The people go just before the heap's last letter, then 'one's' supplies two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin legal phrase means of sound mind, in full control of one's mental faculties.

clue.text: Dictatorial boss of car firm?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a ruler with absolute power
second meaning, playfully: a motor word joined to the Greek ending for a ruler

explanation.surface: A bullying head of a motor company.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a joke split: the first four letters are a word for car.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names an absolute ruler, someone who holds unlimited power and governs alone.

clue.text: Emperor presumably less trustworthy in the West?

parts.words: presumably less trustworthy in the West?
parts.note: setter's reading: the name splits as 'steady in E', so in W, the opposite direction, he would be less steady

explanation.surface: An emperor who could not be relied upon in the western half of his empire.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the name as 'constant in E' (east); fittingly he founded Constantinople, his capital in the east.
explanation.definitionFit: Constantine the Great ruled the Roman empire in the fourth century and moved its capital to Byzantium.

clue.text: Castle, otherwise trapping one knight more in the centre

indicators.note: trapping holds something inside, so the other pieces go within the word for otherwise

parts.note: N is the chess notation for knight

indicators.note: only the middle letters of the last word are kept

explanation.surface: A fortress otherwise holds one more knight at its heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Elsinore is the Danish fortress at Helsingør where Shakespeare set Hamlet.

clue.text: Like sheep, cow loses its head

indicators.note: losing the head means the first letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A cow panics and follows the herd like a sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Ovine is the adjective for sheep, from the Latin ovis, just as bovine relates to cattle.

clue.text: No meat: bread roll for hungry boy

parts.note: liver is offal eaten as meat
a twist is a plaited bread roll

explanation.surface: A meatless meal of just a roll for a famished child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No meat' reads as a menu note but splits into two pieces; this is the Dickens orphan who asked for more.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's workhouse orphan famously asks for more gruel because he is starving.

clue.text: Qualify to start work as surgeon?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: get through to the next round of a competition
second meaning: literally, perform the first incision

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the literal second reading, a surgeon beginning an operation.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf and other contests, players who score well enough survive the elimination stage and progress.

clue.text: Doesn't go across stove with jug

indicators.note: lying across something spans it, so the outer word straddles the rest

parts.note: to stay is not to leave
a range is a cooking stove

explanation.surface: Someone won't walk across the cooker carrying a pitcher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jug' is slang for prison; Strangeways is the famous Victorian prison in Manchester.
explanation.definitionFit: Jug is old slang for a jail, and this is a well-known English prison, so it is one example.

clue.text: Queen, charming, removing a first coat

parts.note: R for Regina, Latin for queen

indicators.note: removing takes a letter away from the word for charming

explanation.surface: A charming queen strips away the first layer of paint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First coat' is not the queen's clothing but a builder's term.
explanation.definitionFit: Rendering is the initial layer of plaster or cement applied to a wall before finishing.

clue.text: Work tongue into part of mouth and be highly successful with what I record

definitions.text: be highly successful with what I record

indicators.note: putting something into a word places it inside

parts.note: the gums are part of the mouth
op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A dentist works a tongue into the mouth and has great success.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is in the voice of a recording artist, whose album sells a million or so copies.
explanation.definitionFit: A record that goes platinum reaches a top sales threshold, a mark of huge commercial success.

clue.text: Fast runner who's barely noticed?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one who moves at great speed, like a flash

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the person rather than a noun
definitions.meaning: second meaning: someone noticed precisely because they are bare, dashing naked across a pitch

explanation.surface: A sprinter who hardly gets seen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barely' seems to mean hardly; it means without clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: This is someone who dashes naked through a public place, such as a sports ground, to draw attention.

clue.text: A mile further, surprising remote Aussie native

indicators.note: something surprising is unexpected, so the letters land in an unexpected order

parts.note: on means further, as in 'and so on'

explanation.surface: A further mile on, an Australian animal turns up in remote country.
explanation.definitionFit: Monotremes, the platypus and echidnas, are egg-laying mammals found only in Australia and New Guinea.

clue.text: Voyager's home, having visited part of moon at end of tour

indicators.note: visiting means going inside, so the word for home sits within the lunar feature

parts.note: a mare is a dark 'sea' on the moon

indicators.note: only the final letter of the last word is wanted

explanation.surface: A space probe's base had passed through a lunar region at the end of its trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Voyager' and 'moon' suggest a space probe; the answer is a seafarer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailor makes sea journeys, so a seafarer is a traveller by water.

clue.text: Pointed remark when one confuses rook with magpie

indicators.note: confusing things mixes them up, so these letters are scrambled together

parts.note: R is the chess notation for rook

explanation.surface: A sharp comment made when a birdwatcher mistakes one black-and-white bird for another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rook' and 'magpie' look like a birdwatching mix-up, but rook is a chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An epigram is a short, witty saying with a sharp twist, a pithy and barbed comment.

clue.text: Born abroad, want to be not too old

explanation.surface: Someone born overseas wants to stay young.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abroad' tells us the word for born is the French one.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fairly recent or almost fresh is only mildly aged, which this suffixed adjective expresses.

clue.text: Manoeuvre bin

definitions.meaning: first meaning: riding a bike on its back wheel alone
second meaning: a large rubbish container on wheels

explanation.walkthrough: 'Manoeuvre bin' looks like an instruction to move the rubbish; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A cyclist's trick of lifting the front tyre is one meaning; the British wheeled refuse container is another.

clue.text: One ruling for now: note the convenience, in short

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
the Gents is a men's toilet, or convenience, here shortened

explanation.surface: A caretaker ruler leaves a note on the public toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a convenience is a public toilet, and the men's is the Gents.
explanation.definitionFit: A regent governs temporarily on behalf of a monarch who is a child, absent or unfit.

clue.text: Agree to study dog

parts.note: to con is to study carefully
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: Consent to research canines.
explanation.definitionFit: To concur is to hold the same opinion, to assent with others.

clue.text: Port or bitter picked up?

indicators.note: to pick something up is to hear it, so we want a word that sounds the same

parts.note: wry means drily mocking or bitter

explanation.surface: A drink order: port or a pint of bitter, collected at the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: Port and bitter look like drinks; Rye is a historic port town in Sussex, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Rye is one of England's medieval Cinque Ports on the Sussex coast, a harbour town.

clue.text: Nowhere is unimportant

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in neither one location nor the other
second meaning: the idiom for something irrelevant

explanation.surface: A statement that location doesn't matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally the phrase means in no place; idiomatically it means of no consequence or irrelevant.

clue.text: Patriarch backing solid husband

indicators.note: going backwards means the word for solid is read in reverse

parts.note: a cone is a solid shape in geometry

explanation.surface: An elder of the family stands behind a dependable husband.
explanation.definitionFit: Enoch is a Genesis figure, father of Methuselah, one of the Bible's ancient founding fathers.

clue.text: Asking more questions about one is not so peaceful

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for asking more questions surrounds the numeral

explanation.surface: Someone who pries more makes the place less tranquil.
explanation.definitionFit: Louder and more disturbing means less quiet, the comparative of a word for loud.

clue.text: Turned up by chance in court

parts.note: a lot is chosen by chance, as in drawing lots

explanation.surface: Someone happened to appear in a courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' suggests law; it is King Arthur's legendary royal seat.
explanation.definitionFit: Camelot is the legendary seat of King Arthur and his knights, the royal household of the Round Table.

clue.text: Strong cloth fine in warm wind

parts.note: chino is a hard-wearing cotton twill

explanation.surface: Sturdy fabric does well when the breeze is warm.
explanation.definitionFit: The chinook is a dry, warm westerly blowing down the eastern Rockies in North America.

clue.text: Mischief-maker's accent not British

indicators.note: 'not British' says the abbreviation for British is removed

parts.note: a brogue is a regional accent, especially Irish

explanation.surface: A troublemaker's way of speaking isn't British.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue is a rascal or scamp, a playfully dishonest person who causes trouble.

clue.text: Painter's assistant is second to be accepted

indicators.note: being accepted means being taken in, so these pieces go inside the assistant word

parts.note: a mate is a helper, as in a plumber's mate

explanation.surface: An artist's helper is next in line for acceptance.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Matisse was the French artist who led the Fauvist movement, famous for colour.

clue.text: One doing exercises, but no header

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone who stretches limbs
second meaning: in bricklaying, a brick laid lengthways, as opposed to one laid end-on

explanation.walkthrough: 'Header' suggests football; in bricklaying a header shows its end and a stretcher its long side.
explanation.definitionFit: Builders lay bricks either end-on or lengthways along a wall, and the long-side brick has this name.
